intro: Driving verbs, road signs, breakdowns, fines and insurance.

palabras.consejo: Before «e» the c becomes «qu»: «arranque». It also means to pull out by the roots.
It comes from «freno». You say «frenar en seco» when you stop suddenly.
It also means doing something ahead of time. On the road it is passing another car.
It means «that goes on and off». You «pones» the intermitente before turning.
In Spain you enter the roundabout giving way to those already inside.
The j sounds like h: «pe-A-he». Toll motorways are paid for; dual carriageways are not.
It is the «Ceda el paso» sign. It also works for people: «cede el paso a los mayores».
You say «ponerse el cinturón». In Spain you must always wear it in the car.
It comes from «pinchar». You say «tener un pinchazo» or «pinchar una rueda».
The accent splits the vowels: «GRU-a». It is also the tall machine on building sites.
The «ll» sounds «y»: «ta-YER». It is also a place for manual work or a practical course.
You say «chocar contra» or «chocar con»: «chocó contra un árbol».
It is also an adjective: «seguro» means «safe». The context makes it clear.
You say «poner una multa» and «pagar una multa». It is feminine: «la multa».
«arrancar» means to start an engine. The «c» before «a» sounds «k»: a-RAN-ka.
«notar» means to notice. The accent marks the final stress: no-TE.
«raro» means unusual. The double «rr» is not needed here: the single «r» at the start is strong.
«repuesto» is masculine: «el repuesto». The «ue» is one sound.
The accent on «pagará» falls on the last syllable: pa-ga-RA.
«no olvides» is a command to not forget. The «v» sounds «b».
«ponerte» means to put on, as clothes or a belt. The «te» is attached.
«exceso» is masculine: «el exceso». Here «exceso de velocidad» means speeding.
«chocar contra» means to crash into. The accent is on the last syllable: cho-KO.
«adelantar» means to overtake a vehicle. The gerund ends in «-ando».
«autovía» is feminine: «la autovía». The «v» is pronounced «b».
«cinta» is feminine: «la cinta». The «c» before «i» sounds «th» in Spain.
«techo» is masculine: «el techo». The «ch» sounds as in «church».
«camión» is masculine: «el camión». The plural is «camiones».
«avanzar» means to move forward. The «z» sounds «th» in Spain.
«lentitud» is feminine: «la lentitud». It comes from «lento», slow.
«elefante» is masculine: «el elefante». The «f» is clear.
«acelerar» means to speed up. The «c» sounds «th» in Spain.
«adelantar» means to overtake. The stress falls on «LAN».
«arcén» is masculine and the stress falls on the last syllable. The «c» is «th».
«hundida» agrees with «rueda», a feminine noun. The «h» is silent.
«encendida» means lit. It agrees with «luces», feminine plural.
«mecánico» is masculine. The accent marks the stress on «CA».
«trapo» is masculine: «el trapo». The «rr» sounds strong at the start.
«frenar» means to brake. The gerund «frenando» describes an action in progress.
«pagas» is the «tú» form. The «g» before «a» is hard.
«infracción» is feminine: «la infracción». Its stress is on «THYON».

texto:
**The verbs.** **Arrancar** the car, **acelerar**, **frenar**, **girar**, **adelantar**, **aparcar**. Before turning, you **pones el intermitente**. You always put on **el cinturón de seguridad**.

**The roads.** **Una autopista** is usually **de peaje**; **una autovía**, not. At a **rotonda** you give way to whoever is already inside. The **Ceda el paso** sign asks for the same.

**When something fails.** You get **un pinchazo**, the engine does not start or you **chocas contra** a tree. **La grúa** comes and takes the car **al taller**.

**The papers.** **El seguro** pays for the damage. If you do something wrong, you get **una multa**.

**Careful.** **Seguro** can be a contract or mean «safe».

piezas.titulo: Iba + gerund, «han puesto» and chocar contra
texto:
**An interrupted action.** To tell of something that was happening when something else occurred: **imperfect + gerund** for the first and **preterite** for the second. **Iba adelantando a un camión cuando noté un golpe.**

**The third person plural with no subject** speaks of people whose identity does not matter: **me han puesto una multa**, **me han quitado tres puntos**. It works like a passive.

**Chocar contra / con** something: **chocó contra un árbol**, **chocaron con otro coche**.

ejemplos.estudio: Me han puesto una multa por exceso de velocidad.
ejemplos.alumno: They have given me a fine for speeding.
analisis: Me han puesto una multa por exceso de velocidad

ejemplos.estudio: Iba adelantando a un camión cuando noté un golpe.
ejemplos.alumno: I was overtaking a lorry when I felt a bump.
analisis: Iba adelantando a un camión cuando noté un golpe

pregunta.texto: What do you do before turning?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: the indicator warns others that you are about to turn.
Adelantar is passing another vehicle, not signalling a turn.
The peaje is paid on the motorway, not before turning.
No: with «chocar» you say «contra» or «con», not «en».
Yes: «chocar contra» is hitting something hard.
With «de» the sentence changes meaning and makes no sense.

frase.texto: El coche no arranca desde esta mañana

piezas.traduccion: The car has not started since this morning

pregunta.texto: What does the tow truck do with a broken-down car?

opciones.explicacion: The fine is given by an officer, not by the tow truck.
The toll is collected on the motorway.
Yes: the grúa carries the broken-down car to the garage.

pregunta.texto: Which tense tells the interrupting action?

frase.texto: Iba frenando cuando ____ un ruido raro.

piezas.traduccion: Iba frenando cuando ____ un ruido raro.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: the preterite tells the one-off moment that interrupts.
The imperfect is for what lasts; here you need the one-off moment.
It is future, but the story has already happened.
A multa is not a part of the car.
